$comment: TDSP 2.0 update vectors: behaviour, not wire — bytes that a receiver of the profile `yjs-paragraphs/1` reads as exactly one update or state vector in Yjs update encoding version 1, or not (Appendix A, "Reading without applying"; §4.4, a frame carrying one that is not is `invalid-field`). Every `update` and `stateVector` is hex. Where a vector puts an item into the top-level type `a`, the update holds one client (1) with one struct at clock 0 whose parent is that type, then an empty delete set. A variable-length integer takes at most 8 bytes and is at most 2^53 − 1. A client's structs end, from the clock of the first by their lengths (a string's in UTF-16 code units), and a delete range ends, its clock plus its length, at most at 2^53 − 1. Nesting counts arrays and objects, the outermost the first level, as §1.6 counts a frame's; each JSON text and each Any value on its own. Checked in src/update-vectors.test.ts.
